doc.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Current plans, self-booking and a George Shearing concert
summary: Jolly describes his upcoming concerts and festivals, booking himself, and a recent Shearing and Joe Williams concert; Rowe wraps up.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What’s coming up in the future for you?

Okay we have some concerts coming up and then the new album we’ll be working on. We just did U of A, University of Arizona, we did a concert over there, and did a concert down in Annenberg Theater down in Palm Springs, and then we’re going to be doing two concerts at a place called the Vintage down in the desert and then another place called — anyway it’s another private club down there. And I’m still trying to get into some more jazz festivals, getting that going. It’s not easy. Like last year I did the Ottawa and I did a short engagement up in San Francisco.
You do your own promotion and booking?

Pretty much, yeah. I don’t really have an agent or a manager. People call and then we make arrangements. I spent a marvelous evening about two weeks ago, George Shearing was playing down at the Studio Center for the Arts, with Joe Williams. And a friend of mine from Cincinnati came out with his daughter and he wanted to see it so he invited me. I had never seen the auditorium but George sounded marvelous. And Don Bagley, the bass player, he went with us. And he remarked, he said, Geez, four people packed this whole place. I said yeah. The drums came out for Joe. Joe did the second half. And that’s the part that really amazes you when you see that many people to come out and see four people. It’s a great concert.
And George sounded marvelous as usual. You know he had some nice stories to tell, some funny stories. He must be what, pushing 80?
Or close, 79, 80? Joe too. Joe sounded great.
Yeah. So you see these guys, they’re filling the places. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
Right. There’s hope for the future. Well I wish you the best of luck in your future endeavors.
It’s been a real pleasure talking to you and I’m anxious to listen to your CD.
